passMeaning: PASS means the F0.2b.5 audit dossier is complete and fail-closed. All three assets remain quarantined and bank/content certification remains blocked.

rows.scope: Census, hashes, directed provenance search, candidate-source availability and deny-by-default disposition for exactly three Matching Headings assets.
rows.findings: 3/3 assets remain unknown-quarantined. Ten web sources were reachable, but exact-match search was directed and non-exhaustive; visible originality and July-2026 academic-review claims remain observed but unverified, and no rights-holder authorization was located.
rows.blockersCarriedForward: Authorship, license, rights-holder authorization, factual sign-off and independent human approval remain unresolved; PASS is not clearance.

rows.scope: Executable identity, registry contract, two-pass review cardinality, source hashes and denial controls for the audit-only delta.
rows.findings: 3 passages, 17 paragraphs, 27 candidate headings and 17 heading decisions are covered exactly; hashes align and all records fail closed without structural registry errors.
rows.blockersCarriedForward: Bank and content certification remain blocked; the public runtime still does not enforce the official no-heading-reuse rule.

rows.scope: Clean first-pass main-idea adjudication followed by direct candidate-source review; no stored key was shown before decisions were fixed.
rows.findings: 17/17 heading decisions match the stored mappings, with 0 material ambiguities. All three passage assessments are mixed because the tasks are easier and more predictable than a strong live-style IELTS set.
rows.blockersCarriedForward: Agreement is not approval: explicit topic sentences, close lexical echoes, extreme distractors, factual-risk findings and the missing runtime no-reuse enforcement require editorial repair and fresh blind review.

rows.scope: Prospective content-only simulation by an average learner who recognizes lexical-matching and local-detail failure modes.
rows.findings: 3/3 passages and 17/17 paragraphs have a walkthrough covering global reading, main-idea compression, heading comparison, competitor rejection and a repair action without assigning a key.
rows.blockersCarriedForward: This AI walkthrough is not a real-user usability study, retention measure, learning-gain estimate or evidence of IELTS band improvement.

rows.scope: Exhaustive n=17 enumeration of response labels, sequence, position, option length, lexical overlap, extreme cues, set-level reuse, title risk, representation, prior knowledge and packet leakage.
rows.findings: Stored counts are i=3, ii=0, iii=3, iv=2, v=2, vi=1, vii=2, viii=2, ix=2; same-position scores 5/17, lexical overlap scores 6/14 eligible with 3 ties, and nine options trigger the extreme-cue heuristic: eight are never correct and one is a legitimate contextual use.
rows.blockersCarriedForward: contentCertification remains blocked: n=17 is below 100, ii is never correct, lexical overlap is predictive when unique, extreme wording marks eight distractors, and runtime no-reuse is absent.
